APT-ENG-0451: The error lies in the misspelled word 'knowlege'. Option A provides the correct spelling: 'knowledge'. Correct sentence: 'Man has made many changes on earth with primitive tools and limited knowledge.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0452: Option C contains an adverb-usage error: 'analysed careful'. The passive verb 'were analysed' must be modified by the adverb of manner 'carefully', not the adjective 'careful'. Correct sentence: 'The results were analysed carefully to ensure accuracy.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0453: Option C correctly rectifies the error. The past publication date 'In its August 1992 issue' requires the simple past tense 'described' rather than the present tense 'describe'. Correct sentence: 'In its August 1992 issue, the highly respected British Journal of Addiction described three unusual cases of carrot dependence.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0454: The error lies in segment (C) 'from childhood'. When denoting a state that began in the past and continues into the present, the preposition 'since' is used for a point of origin: 'since childhood', not 'from childhood'. Correct sentence: 'I never miss a cricket match as I am fond of cricket since childhood.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0455: The error lies in segment (C) 'Would you liked'. The modal auxiliary verb 'Would' must be followed by the base form of the verb (bare infinitive V1 'like'), not the past form 'liked'. Correct sentence: '“Would you like to have some fries along with your coffee, sir?” asked the waiter.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0456: The error lies in part (2) 'very reckless'. The verb 'drives' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('very recklessly'), not an adjective ('reckless'). Correct sentence: 'He drives very recklessly on the highway, ignoring all traffic rules.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0457: The error lies in part (2) 'of the delay and'. The verb 'apologise' takes the preposition 'for' when referring to the reason for an apology ('apologised for the delay'), not 'of'. Correct sentence: 'She apologised for the delay and promised to submit the report soon.' Part (2) corresponds to option D. Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0458: The error lies in part (3) 'and to paint landscapes'. Grammatical parallelism requires elements in a coordinated list governed by 'enjoys' to take the same gerund form: 'reading novels, listening to music, and painting landscapes'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0459: The error lies in part (2) 'for ensuring that all members'. The adjective 'committed' takes the preposition 'to' followed by a gerund ('committed to ensuring'), not 'for'. Correct sentence: 'The committee is committed to ensuring that all members have an equal opportunity...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0460: The error lies in part (2) 'is reviewed by an independent expert'. In formal English, clauses following verbs of recommendation ('recommended that...') use the mandative subjunctive mood with the base form 'be reviewed', not the indicative 'is reviewed'. Correct sentence: 'The committee recommended that the proposal be reviewed by an independent expert...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0461: The error lies in part (1) 'explained about the revised procedures'. The verb 'explain' is a transitive verb that takes a direct object without the preposition 'about'. Correct sentence: 'The coordinator carefully explained the revised procedures to all the participants...' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0462: The error lies in part (2) 'were praised'. When a subject is joined to another noun by parenthetical phrases like 'as well as', 'together with', or 'along with', the verb agrees strictly with the first subject ('The main actor', singular), requiring 'was praised'. Correct sentence: 'The main actor, as well as the supporting cast, was praised for their outstanding performance in the play.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0463: The error lies in part (3) 'but it also rises concerns'. 'Rise' is an intransitive verb meaning to go up. The transitive verb meaning to bring up or provoke an issue is 'raises' ('raises concerns'). Correct sentence: '...but it also raises concerns about data privacy and ethical implications.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0464: The error lies in part (3) 'their reports before'. The distributive antecedent 'each participant' is grammatically singular and formally requires the singular pronoun 'his or her report' rather than the plural 'their reports'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0465: The error lies in part (3) 'makes its successful completion'. The subject of the sentence is the plural noun 'The unique challenges', which takes the plural verb 'make', not the singular form 'makes'. Correct sentence: 'The unique challenges of the project... make its successful completion a testament to the team's resilience.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0466: The error lies in part (3) 'was convinced'. When subjects are connected by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees in number with the nearer subject ('the producers', plural), which requires the plural verb 'were convinced'. Correct sentence: 'Neither the director nor the producers were convinced by the proposed revisions.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0467: The error lies in part (2) 'who is always ready'. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural antecedent 'people' in the construction 'one of those people who...', requiring the plural verb 'are always ready'. Correct sentence: 'She is one of those people who are always ready to help.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0468: The error lies in part (2) 'was analysed'. In scientific and academic usage, 'data' is treated as a plural noun (plural of 'datum'), taking the plural verb 'were analysed'. Correct sentence: 'The data collected from various sources were analysed thoroughly.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0469: The error lies in part (2) 'than the audience'. The negative adverb 'Scarcely' pairs with the correlative conjunction 'when', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'Scarcely had she finished speaking when the audience applauded enthusiastically.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0470: The error lies in part (2) 'on to pay the bill'. The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' followed by a gerund ('insisted on paying'), not an infinitive with 'to'. Correct sentence: 'He insisted on paying the bill for everyone.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0471: The error lies in part (2) 'have decreased'. The subject 'The number of + plural noun' is singular and takes the singular verb 'has decreased', unlike 'A number of' which takes a plural verb. Correct sentence: 'The number of accidents has decreased significantly this year.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0472: The error lies in part (1) 'Despite of the heavy rain'. The preposition 'Despite' does not take 'of'; it directly governs a noun phrase ('Despite the heavy rain') or can be replaced by 'In spite of'. Correct sentence: 'Despite the heavy rain, they continued the match.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0473: The error lies in part (2) 'than all her peers'. Comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' (senior, junior, superior) take the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'She is senior to all her peers in experience.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0474: The error lies in part (2) 'were awarded'. When nouns joined by 'and' are each preceded by 'each' or 'every', the compound subject takes a singular verb ('was awarded'). Correct sentence: 'Each boy and each girl was awarded a medal.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0475: The error lies in part (2) 'when the phone rang'. The correlative pair with 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. Correct sentence: 'No sooner did he arrive than the phone rang.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0476: The error lies in part (2) 'has arrested'. The noun 'police' is a plural collective noun that requires the plural auxiliary verb 'have arrested'. Correct sentence: 'The police have arrested the culprit.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0477: The error lies in part (3) 'as if he was king'. Hypothetical or unreal conditions introduced by 'as if' take the past subjunctive 'were', not 'was'. Correct sentence: 'He behaves as if he were king.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0478: The error lies in part (1) 'Unless you do not tell'. The conjunction 'Unless' already contains negation ('if not'); adding 'do not' creates an erroneous double negative. Correct sentence: 'Unless you tell the truth, no one will believe you.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0479: The error lies in part (2) 'than coffee'. The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to' when expressing a preference between two items, not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'I prefer tea to coffee.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0480: The error lies in part (2) 'are essential'. When two nouns joined by 'and' represent a single composite dish or idea ('Bread and butter'), the subject takes the singular verb 'is'. Correct sentence: 'Bread and butter is essential for breakfast.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0481: The error lies in part (1) 'She don't know'. The third-person singular pronoun 'She' takes the singular negative auxiliary 'doesn't', not 'don't'. Correct sentence: 'She doesn't know the answer.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0482: The error lies in part (2) 'is because'. The construction 'The reason why... is because' is redundant; the correct copular complement is 'is that...'. Correct sentence: 'The reason why he failed is that he was negligent.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0483: The error lies in segment (B) 'By virtue off'. The standard prepositional idiom meaning by authority of or on account of is 'By virtue of' (with a single 'f'), not 'off'. Correct sentence: 'By virtue of the power given to the leader, the followers accepted his decision.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0484: The error lies in segment (D) 'an hurry'. The noun 'hurry' begins with a consonant sound (/h/), requiring the indefinite article 'a' rather than 'an' in the fixed idiom 'in a hurry'. Correct sentence: 'She is in a hurry to meet her brother.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0485: The error lies in segment (B) 'is not enough big to meet'. When 'enough' modifies an adjective, it must be placed immediately after the adjective: 'is not big enough', not 'enough big'. Correct sentence: 'The food container is not big enough to meet the demands of the affected people.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0486: The error lies in segment (A) 'interfere in'. Following the past perfect auxiliary 'had', the main verb must appear in its past participle form (V3 'interfered'), not the base form 'interfere'. Correct sentence: 'Sajni had interfered in this matter.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0487: The error lies in segment (C) 'a place you recommended'. A specific location that has already been identified and recommended by the interlocutor requires the definite article 'the', not 'a'. Correct sentence: 'I brought an apple from the place you recommended me earlier.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0488: The error lies in segment (D) 'the postman would be'. The main clause expressing present confidence ('I am sure that') takes the future continuous indicative 'will be coming', not the conditional modal 'would be'. Correct sentence: 'I am sure that the postman will be coming shortly to deliver the letter.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0489: The error lies in segment (A) 'The five first girls'. In English numeral order, ordinal numbers (first, second) precede cardinal numbers (one, five): 'The first five girls', not 'five first'. Correct sentence: 'The first five girls will get the discount on our merchandise.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0490: The error lies in segment (D) 'The investigation conducting by the research team'. The passive participial modifier describing the investigation carried out by the team must be the past participle 'conducted', not the active present participle 'conducting'. Correct sentence: 'The investigation conducted by the research team yielded statistically significant results...' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0491: The error lies in segment (B) 'at five on the morning'. The standard preposition for periods of the day is 'in': 'in the morning', not 'on the morning'. Correct sentence: 'They will go to bed early since they have to get up at five in the morning.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0492: The error lies in segment (C) 'to is open of learning more,'. The adjective 'open' collocates with the preposition 'to' followed by a gerund ('open to learning more'), not 'of'. Correct sentence: 'If someone you are talking to is open to learning more, encourage that continued curiosity.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0493: The error lies in segment (D) 'fairly criticises'. The adverb 'fairly' (moderately/tolerably) is inappropriate for a serious commentary; an intensifier like 'severely', 'sharply', or 'rightly' is required to convey substantive critique. Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0494: The error lies in segment (D) 'undergraduate days were'. The grammatical subject of the sentence is the singular pronoun 'One' ('One of the major challenges...'), which takes the singular verb 'was', not the plural 'were'. Correct sentence: 'One of the major challenges he faced during his undergraduate days was the shortage of money.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0495: Option D contains the error in 'at the classroom'. For an enclosed room or space, the preposition 'in' is used ('in the classroom'), not 'at'. Correct sentence: 'There are no tables in the classroom.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0496: The error lies in segment (A) 'but returned back'. The verb 'return' inherently means 'to go back' or 'to come back'; adding 'back' creates an erroneous pleonasm. Correct sentence: 'He went to work but returned immediately.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0497: The error lies in part (2) 'were ready for the sudden fire drill'. When subjects are connected by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees in number with the nearer subject ('the teacher', singular), requiring 'was ready', not 'were ready'. Correct sentence: 'Neither the students nor the teacher was ready for the sudden fire drill...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0498: The error lies in part (3) 'but also it was thoroughly tested'. Parallelism with the correlative conjunction 'not only... but also' requires balancing adjectives: 'not only innovative but also thoroughly tested', without repeating the subject and verb 'it was'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0499: The error lies in part (3) 'to foster a sense of community'. Grammatical parallelism requires elements in a coordinated series to share the same grammatical form; following 'increasing' and 'improving', the third item must be the gerund 'fostering', not the infinitive 'to foster'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0500: The error lies in part (1) 'which oversee multiple departments'. The relative pronoun 'which' refers to the singular noun 'The committee', which requires the singular verb 'oversees' in the simple present tense, not the base form 'oversee'. Correct sentence: 'The committee, which oversees multiple departments...' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0501: The error lies in part (2) 'often demands'. The subject of the sentence is 'The myriad challenges' (plural), which requires the plural verb 'demand', not the singular 'demands'. Correct sentence: 'The myriad challenges confronting modern urban planners... often demand an interdisciplinary approach...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0502: The error lies in part (2) 'and promoting critical scholarship'. Parallelism with the correlative structure 'to both... and...' requires matching base verb forms: 'to both preserve ancient texts and promote critical scholarship', not 'promoting'. Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0503: The error lies in segment (A) 'already began'. The past perfect tense requires the auxiliary 'had' followed by the past participle (V3) form 'begun', not the simple past 'began'. Correct sentence: 'When I reached the cinema hall, the movie had already begun.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0504: Option D contains an adverb-usage error: 'Quickly does he watch television.'. The adverb of manner 'quickly' cannot initiate subject-auxiliary inversion with 'watch television'; a frequency adverb like 'Rarely' or 'Seldom' is required ('Seldom does he watch television'). Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0505: The error lies in segment (D) 'I are dancing'. The first-person singular pronoun 'I' takes the auxiliary verb 'am', not 'are'. Correct sentence: 'I am dancing with my husband at my sister’s wedding.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0506: Option D correctly rectifies the error. In the passive modal construction 'should not be + past participle', the verb must take the past participle form 'written', not the base form 'write'. Correct sentence: 'As a rule, single sentences should not be written or printed as paragraphs.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0507: Option B correctly rectifies the error. The narrative is set in the past ('greeted us', 'had learned'), requiring the simple past tense 'saw' rather than the present tense 'sees'. Correct sentence: 'He saw us coming, and unaware that we had learned of his treachery, greeted us with a smile.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0508: The error lies in segment (B) 'as her'. The clause requires a subject pronoun ('she') and a temporal conjunction ('when'): 'when she was 23', not 'as her was 23'. Correct sentence: 'My sister, Juliet, got married when she was 23.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0509: The error lies in segment (D) 'the book everywhere'. In a negative sentence ('cannot find'), the negative polarity item 'anywhere' must be used rather than 'everywhere'. Correct sentence: 'I cannot find the book anywhere in the house; it seems to have disappeared.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0510: The error lies in part (1) 'A large number of equipments'. The noun 'equipment' is uncountable in English and cannot take the plural suffix '-s'; it should be 'pieces of equipment'. Correct sentence: 'A large amount of equipment / A large number of pieces of equipment were delivered...' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0511: The error lies in part (3) 'further informations is received'. The noun 'information' is uncountable and cannot be pluralized as 'informations'; it should be 'further information is received'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0512: The error lies in part (2) 'were overly optimistic'. The subject of the clause is 'its interpretation' (singular), which takes the singular verb 'was overly optimistic', not the plural 'were'. Correct sentence: '...but that its interpretation by the junior analysts was overly optimistic...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0513: The error lies in part (2) 'were prepared in haste'. The subject is 'The list' (singular), which requires the singular auxiliary verb 'was prepared', not the plural 'were'. Correct sentence: 'The list of recommended candidates for various regional posts was prepared in haste...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0514: The error lies in part (2) 'many important informations'. 'Information' is an uncountable noun that cannot be pluralized or quantified with 'many'; it should be 'much important information' or 'many pieces of important information'. Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0515: The error lies in part (3) 'that allows scientists to conduct'. The relative pronoun 'that' refers to the plural antecedent 'instruments', requiring the plural verb 'allow', not the singular 'allows'. Correct sentence: '...instruments that allow scientists to conduct complex molecular experiments.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0516: The error lies in part (3) 'were surprising'. The phrase 'The number of + plural noun' takes a singular verb ('was surprising'), unlike 'A number of' which takes a plural verb. Correct sentence: 'The number of participants in the advanced workshop was surprising...' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0517: The error lies in part (2) 'are viable'. The distributive pronoun 'Neither' is grammatically singular and takes the singular verb 'is viable', not 'are'. Correct sentence: 'Neither of the two solutions is viable.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0518: The error lies in part (2) 'have visited the site'. When a subject is joined to another noun by 'accompanied by', the verb agrees with the primary subject ('The CEO', singular), requiring 'has visited', not 'have'. Correct sentence: 'The CEO, accompanied by senior directors, has visited the site.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0519: The error lies in part (2) 'meeting began when'. Following the past perfect auxiliary 'had', the verb must take its past participle form 'begun', not the simple past 'began'. Correct sentence: 'Hardly had the meeting begun when the power went out.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0520: The error lies in part (2) 'superior than all her peers'. Comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' take the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'She is superior to all her peers in dedication.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0521: The error lies in part (2) 'major problem in urban areas'. The partitive phrase 'one of the + plural noun' requires 'problems'. Correct sentence: 'One of the major problems in urban areas is pollution.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0522: The error lies in part (2) 'were divided in its decision'. When acting with a singular reference ('its decision'), the collective noun takes the singular verb 'was divided'. Correct sentence: 'The committee was divided in its decision.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0523: The error lies in part (3) 'since three days'. A duration of time ('three days') takes the preposition 'for', not 'since'. Correct sentence: 'He has been ill for three days.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0524: The error lies in part (1) 'Unless you do not practice'. 'Unless' already means 'if not'; using 'do not' creates an erroneous double negative. Correct sentence: 'Unless you practice regularly, you will not improve.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0525: The error lies in part (2) 'in the office are expensive'. The uncountable noun 'furniture' takes the singular verb 'is', not 'are'. Correct sentence: 'The furniture in the office is expensive.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0526: The error lies in part (2) 'did not accepted'. Following the auxiliary 'did not', the main verb must appear in its base form 'accept', not the past tense 'accepted'. Correct sentence: 'He did not accept the proposal.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0527: The error lies in part (2) 'The news are very alarming'. The noun 'news' is uncountable and takes the singular verb 'is', not 'are'. Correct sentence: 'The news is very alarming.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0528: The error lies in part (3) 'their own laptop'. The singular antecedent 'Each student' grammatically requires the singular possessive determiner 'his or her own laptop'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0529: The error lies in part (2) 'entered the hall than'. Following the auxiliary 'did', the main verb must appear in its base form 'enter', not the past tense 'entered'. Correct sentence: 'No sooner did she enter the hall than the performance began.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0530: The error lies in part (1) 'The police is investigating'. The collective noun 'police' is plural and takes the plural verb 'are investigating', not 'is'. Correct sentence: 'The police are investigating the case.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0531: The error lies in part (2) 'prefer tea than coffee'. The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'I prefer tea to coffee.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0532: The error lies in part (1) 'Ten miles are a long journey'. A distance regarded as a single measurement or unit takes the singular verb 'is'. Correct sentence: 'Ten miles is a long journey.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0533: Option C correctly rectifies the sentence. The future periphrastic idiom is 'be going to + V1', which takes 'is going to call', not the ungrammatical hybrid 'will going to call'. Correct sentence: 'Bakshi is going to call you later in the evening.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0534: The error lies in segment (C) 'to buy a expensive car'. The adjective 'expensive' begins with a vowel sound (/ɪ/), which requires the indefinite article 'an' rather than 'a'. Segment (C) corresponds to option A. Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0535: The error lies in segment (C) 'I dry the same'. Using 'the same' as a pronoun for everyday objects is archaic and unidiomatic; the personal pronoun 'them' should be used ('and I'll dry them'). Correct sentence: 'You wash the dishes and I will dry them.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0536: The error lies in segment (B) 'They were laid'. The intransitive verb meaning to recline in the past tense is 'lay' ('They lay in the sun'), whereas 'laid' is the past tense of the transitive verb 'lay' (to place something). Correct sentence: 'They lay in the sun the entire morning till Sudharshan came.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0537: The error lies in segment (C) 'Were this boy'. The singular subject 'this boy' requires the singular past auxiliary verb 'Was', not the plural 'Were'. Correct sentence: 'Was this boy washing his clothes yesterday when the matron came for a regular round?' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0538: The error lies in segment (B) 'divided on groups,'. The verb 'divide' takes the preposition 'into' when separating into parts or sections ('divided into groups'), not 'on'. Correct sentence: 'The young learners were divided into groups, according to their abilities.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0539: The error lies in segment (B) 'for he had neither gun or spear.'. The correlative pair with 'neither' is 'nor', not 'or' ('neither gun nor spear'). Correct sentence: '...for he had neither gun nor spear.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0540: The error lies in segment (C) 'for a opportunity'. The noun 'opportunity' begins with a vowel sound (/ɒ/), requiring the indefinite article 'an' rather than 'a'. Correct sentence: 'She was waiting for an opportunity to start her own business.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0541: The error lies in segment (D) 'Fashion might not be first'. The ordinal number 'first' modifying a singular countable noun requires the definite article 'the': 'the first thing'. Correct sentence: 'Fashion might not be the first thing that comes to mind...' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0542: The error lies in segment (D) 'Every of the two'. Correct sentence: 'Each of the two girls will get the reward.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0544: The error lies in segment (D) 'invite me'. The third-person singular pronoun 'She' with the frequency adverb 'always' takes the simple present singular verb 'invites', not 'invite'. Correct sentence: 'She always invites me to dinner.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0545: The error lies in segment (B) 'Robert come to clean the stable'. APT-ENG-0547: The error lies in segment (B) 'the world's leading string quartet.'. The partitive phrase 'one of the + superlative + plural noun' requires the plural form 'string quartets'. Correct sentence: '...is one of the world's leading string quartets.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0548: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. 'Mother said that it was quite all right for her to get upset for scoring less' is grammatically sound. Hence, option B ('No error') is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0550: The error lies in segment (A) 'accused for stealing'. The verb 'accuse' collocates with the preposition 'of', not 'for' ('accused of stealing'). Correct sentence: 'The prisoner was accused of stealing from his landlord.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
